sermon.title: BASING YOUR FAITH On THE POWER of GOD 12/3/2017
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: Pastor David G. Kincer asks what your faith is based on and answers from 1 Corinthians 2: not human wisdom or apologetics but the demonstration of the Spirit and power. He points to Abraham’s full persuasion, the gospel of Christ crucified, the power to live a moral life, and Mark 16’s signs following believers—illustrated with demonic encounters and God’s protection on the mission field.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added from the speaker’s pauses and then corrected by hand, and obvious caption errors (names, Bible references) were fixed; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: Congregants and the interpreter’s family are named in the transcript only. Points to check: Supreme Court ruling that atheism is a religion; “only thirty percent” in Pentecostal and charismatic churches speak in tongues; “over 100 apologists”; book titles as spoken. Sensitive content kept as spoken: personal claims about Josh McDowell’s beliefs (Holy Ghost, Genesis 6, pre-tribulation rapture) and Lee Strobel; Catholic “idols”, ritualistic services; Christians on Facebook “talk nonsense”; apologists who drop baptism “pass this nonsense on”; demonic manifestations and witch doctors; drinking mouthwash (“if I had whiskey there”) to kill a mouth fungus; guerrillas shooting into a church meeting in El Salvador; divorce, drunkenness, drugs in Catholic and Protestant churches; welfare.

scriptures.text_nkjv: And they went out and preached everywhere, the Lord working with them and confirming the word through the accompanying signs. Amen.

Love suffers long and is kind; love does not envy; love does not parade itself, is not puffed up; does not behave rudely, does not seek its own, is not provoked, thinks no evil; does not rejoice in iniquity, but rejoices in the truth; bears all things, believes all things, hopes all things, endures all things.
